topic: Constructive all-alphabet sharpness of multivalued conjunction probabilities of causation. For finite X with m treatment levels and finite potential outcomes with r labels, consistency, and compatible common-population observational and one-treatment intervention margins, prove the published Shu–Wang–Li scalar conjunction bounds are attained for every real input. Derive an exact indicator coarsening and categorical lifting; construct the upper endpoint by intersection packing and the lower endpoint by a complete bipartite max-flow with diagonal edges removed and a proved residual-failure filling invariant; show mixtures fill the entire identified interval. For rational input give O(mr+k log k) endpoint evaluation, polynomial-time polynomial-support exact primal SCM laws, active-affine/min-cut dual certificates, and audited bit complexity. Add polynomial-size block-multinomial confidence-region inversion with uniform finite-sample coverage, while crediting Cheng–Mao–Pearl–Li for directional inference. Position against Shu–Wang–Li, binary-only Xie–Li, generic response-signature LPs, and Harinen et al. as a common-population hypothetical customer-journey consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Two score-blind presolves independently derived the categorical lifting, intersection packing, diagonal-deleted cut formula, and the unused-capacity residual invariant. Fresh exact arithmetic reproduced every full categorical margin and endpoint in 954 laws, including zero rows, deterministic p_i=1 boundaries, the five-way tie, and m=40,r=3,k=30; 97,625 subset/positive-part configurations and 80 confidence-program comparisons found no failure. Unequal alphabets, repeated queried labels, k<m, proper/full subset cuts, and global/singleton lower cuts were explicitly exercised. Searches found no collision with the disclosed binary, partial-diagram, generic-LP, or inference follow-ups. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently formalize the finite-cell TAKE refinement lemma and audit polynomial support, denominator, and bit-complexity accounting across all zero-mass domains; no central theorem step is being assumed. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the singleton-lower, proper-subset-upper, five-way-tie, and p_i=1 endpoint laws with exact arithmetic and verify every observational/interventional cell, objective, and residual-failure invariant; any failure stops this framing. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_multivalued_poc_flow_sharpness.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary finite treatment alphabet m, outcome alphabet r, and conjunction length k ≤ m—including unequal alphabets and repeated queried labels—are the Shu–Wang–Li conjunction-PNS bounds pointwise sharp for every compatible real vector of common-population observational and single-treatment interventional margins?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves validity in general dimensions, supports tightness through low-dimensional computation, and leaves a complete all-dimensional tightness proof open.
source_refs.author: Xin Shu, Shuai Wang, and Ang Li

source_refs.claim: The paper constructively proves binary PNS tightness and identifies nonnegative solvability of enlarged response-type systems as the obstacle to nonbinary extension.
source_refs.author: Yuxuan Xie and Ang Li
source_refs.venue: Causality for Decision Making Workshop at UAI 2026

open_problems.why_unsolved: Validity of each affine endpoint does not provide an endpoint-attaining SCM for every feasible margin vector. Xie–Li's active-region construction resolves only the eight-cell binary system, while direct response-signature LPs grow exponentially and do not yield a uniform nonnegative filling argument. The presolve's categorical lifting, diagonal-deleted flow, and residual-capacity construction remain hypotheses until the finite-cell TAKE refinement lemma and the zero-mass, support, denominator, and bit-complexity cases are proved independently.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact characterization of the identified interval with explicit finite-support SCM laws attaining both endpoints for every compatible real input, a mixture argument filling the interval, and polynomial-time rational-input primal and dual certificates with audited support and bit bounds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from binary attribution to representative discrete conjunctions and then to closed-form bounds is the natural motivation arc to continue with universal attainability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Individual attribution requires joint counterfactual probabilities -> multivalued decisions create higher-order conjunctions -> closed-form bounds make evaluation practical -> universal endpoint-attaining constructions are still required to certify sharpness.

method_exemplars.technique: Partition the observable-margin space by the active affine bound and explicitly solve the response-type equations with nonnegative masses in every region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the same every-input attainability property for binary PNS; the new proof must replace its finite case split with an all-alphabet coupling or flow invariant.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the equivalence between finite Strassen coupling conditions, Hall inequalities, and matching or flow feasibility, representing coupling deficiency by cut slack.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed lower endpoint is a categorical coupling with forbidden diagonal coincidences, making diagonal-deleted flow feasibility and min-cut certificates structurally analogous.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent bound endpoints as finite affine envelopes and derive regular or directionally differentiable limit laws from their active sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once sharpness identifies the endpoint with the published piecewise-affine expression, this is the closest available route from multinomial margin estimators to tie-aware endpoint inference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the sharp all-alphabet conjunction-PNS interval be equipped with polynomial-size confidence-region inversion having uniform finite-sample coverage over every compatible block-multinomial law, including zero cells and multiple active affine terms?

source_refs.claim: The paper derives ordinary delta-method inference under a unique active term and directional non-Gaussian limits at ties; its guarantees are asymptotic and its worked PoC cases are binary.
source_refs.author: Tianyuan Cheng, Ruirui Mao, Judea Pearl, and Ang Li

source_refs.claim: The paper gives finite-sample coverage-error bounds for optimization-defined partially identified parameters but does not specialize them to exact block-multinomial PoC inversion.
source_refs.author: Joel L. Horowitz and Sokbae Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: The endpoint map is nonsmooth when affine terms tie, so a single-gradient Gaussian interval is not uniformly valid near active-set changes. Directional asymptotics do not themselves provide finite-sample uniform coverage, and zero-probability cells put multinomial parameters on simplex faces where plug-in covariance matrices are singular. Generic partial-identification inference does not exploit the explicit affine-envelope and block-multinomial structure to obtain a polynomial-size exact or concentration-calibrated inversion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-description block-multinomial confidence set and endpoint-optimization procedure with a proof of at least 1−α simultaneous coverage uniformly over the complete compatible simplex, including boundary cells, interval collapse, and arbitrary active-term ties.

writing_exemplar.why: Its direct transition from population PoC bounds to sampling uncertainty and its separation of unique-active and tied-active regimes should be retained while finite-sample uniformity becomes the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sharp PoC formulas are population objects -> their margins are estimated from separate samples -> affine maxima and minima create nondifferentiable ties -> finite-sample inversion is needed at ties and simplex boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the endpoint directional derivative as an extremum of correlated Gaussian linear forms indexed by the population active set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the asymptotic benchmark that a uniformly valid finite-sample construction must recover without losing correctness at multiway ties.

method_exemplars.technique: Enlarge an optimization problem using a confidence set for its unknown moments and transfer moment-set containment into a nonasymptotic coverage guarantee.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The PoC endpoints are optimization values depending on finitely many multinomial means, so the same containment proof can support exact or concentration-based blockwise inversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct confidence intervals for interval-identified scalar parameters that remain valid as the identification-region width approaches zero.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The conjunction-PNS interval may collapse or nearly collapse, so width-uniform reasoning is needed after endpoint uncertainty is incorporated.

open_problems.open_problem: Are the Shu–Wang–Li bounds for multivalued substitute, replacement, and necessity probabilities pointwise sharp for arbitrary finite alphabets once their additional factual-treatment or factual-outcome constraints are imposed?

source_refs.claim: The paper reduces discrete PoCs to representative PNS, substitute, replacement, and necessity families and gives closed-form bounds without a complete general-dimensional attainability proof.
source_refs.author: Xin Shu, Shuai Wang, and Ang Li

source_refs.claim: After proving binary PNS tightness, the paper names extension to nonbinary PoCs and the complete representative class as future work.
source_refs.author: Yuxuan Xie and Ang Li
source_refs.venue: Causality for Decision Making Workshop at UAI 2026

source_refs.claim: The earlier nonbinary theory gives recursive bounds and states that most are not known to be tight.
source_refs.author: Ang Li and Judea Pearl

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conjunction PNS requires coupling potential-outcome labels, whereas substitute and necessity targets also pin realized treatment and replacement and necessity targets pin realized outcome. Consistency therefore couples response signatures to factual cells, changing the first construction step. Neither the published validity proof nor the binary active-region construction supplies a nonnegative residual-filling invariant for those extra factual slices, and fixed-alphabet response-type LPs do not determine the universal failure frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: For each representative family, an endpoint-attainment characterization that either constructs compatible SCM laws for every feasible margin vector or supplies an explicit counterexample regime and corrected sharp bound, while identifying exactly which factual-cell constraints obstruct the conjunction coupling.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing cleanly separates bound validity from pointwise tightness and explains why attainability determines whether users need stronger assumptions or sharper mathematics.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PoCs are generally only bounded -> valid but nonsharp intervals can misdirect decisions -> binary PNS now has an every-margin construction -> the remaining multivalued representative families need the same certification.

method_exemplars.technique: Use equivalence classes and value-replaceability to reduce arbitrary discrete PoCs to representative objectives before analyzing their affine bound terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result should prove or refute sharpness once per representative objective and transfer it across value permutations.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct nonnegative response-type masses conditional on the active affine bound and prove that the active regions cover the feasible observable space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination asks for the same pointwise-attainment property, but the construction must preserve additional realized-treatment or realized-outcome slices.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply active-affine directional delta analysis to extrema of linear or linear-fractional PoC bound components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the corrected sharp bounds remain finite affine envelopes, this supplies a concrete tie-aware estimator and limit-law rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one obtain sharp closed-form or polynomial-size flow-and-cut bounds for multivalued conjunction PNS when observational or interventional margins are available only for selected subpopulations?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves tight incomplete-subpopulation bounds for binary variables and identifies the nonbinary response-type program and its closed-form solution as future work.
source_refs.author: Yuxuan Xie and Ang Li

open_problems.why_unsolved: The binary formulas exploit a small response table and a simple decomposition between observed and missing subgroups. With multivalued treatments, outcomes, and subgroup labels, response signatures grow exponentially and population mass must be allocated jointly across subgroup-specific factual and counterfactual margins. The published binary construction does not provide a layered categorical-flow invariant, and numerical LP formulations do not identify when partial subgroup information is informative or yield compact endpoint witnesses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact sharp endpoint formula or equivalent polynomial-size max-flow/min-cut program for each specified missing-subpopulation regime, with endpoint-attaining SCM laws and a necessary-and-sufficient condition for source-subpopulation margins to tighten the target-subpopulation interval.

writing_exemplar.why: Its data-availability framing moves directly from practical missing-subpopulation patterns to informative versus vacuous bounds and naturally exposes the multivalued destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PoCs combine experimental and observational margins -> real datasets cover only selected subpopulations -> binary theory shows when partial margins remain informative -> multivalued conjunctions need scalable sharp bounds and an exact noninformativeness frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce arbitrary discrete conjunction queries to representative forms and express baseline bounds as finite affine envelopes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The incomplete-subpopulation result must reduce to these common-population endpoints when every subgroup margin is observed.

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize finite coupling existence through Hall inequalities and construct feasible couplings by matching or flow.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Allocating observed and missing subgroup mass subject to categorical margins is a layered finite-coupling problem whose failures can be represented by cut deficiencies.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate finite affine bound envelopes and derive active-set limit laws from separately sampled observational and experimental margins.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If incomplete-data endpoints have a finite cut dual, its active cuts provide a direct estimation-and-inference rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Under what checkable partial-diagram conditions can mediator information for multivalued conjunction PNS be represented by a polynomial-size linear or convex program with sharp SCM-attained extrema rather than a nonconvex bilinear response-type program?

source_refs.claim: The mediator formulation introduces bilinear conditional-independence equalities and calls for lower-dimensional summaries, alternative linear parameterizations, or certified tractable relaxations.
source_refs.author: Yuxuan Xie and Ang Li

source_refs.claim: The paper derives multivalued PoC bounds using covariate and mediator knowledge, leaving a live sharpness-versus-tractability frontier beyond the common-population base model.
source_refs.author: Xin Shu, Zhen Lei, and Ang Li

open_problems.why_unsolved: Common-population margin sharpness is linear in response-type masses, but mediator restrictions introduce products of marginal sums through cross-world conditional independences. This changes the first proof step by making the feasible set nonconvex and susceptible to local optima. Existing finite-alphabet programs expose the bilinear obstacle but do not identify an assumption class under which mediator coarsening preserves the exact PoC identified set and restores certified polynomial-time optimization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sufficient-condition characterization of mediator structures for which a stated coarsening or reparameterization converts the bilinear restrictions into an equivalent polynomial-size linear or convex feasible set, together with sharpness and endpoint-attainment proofs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its practical progression from incomplete causal knowledge to modular constraints and its contrast between tractable covariate programs and nonconvex mediator programs directly frames the destination.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Complete causal diagrams are rarely available -> partial covariate and mediator knowledge can tighten PoC bounds -> mediator independences create bilinear programs -> exact tractable summaries require a structural characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate graph-supplied covariate and mediator restrictions into constraints on counterfactual response distributions and compare their induced bounds with the baseline Tian–Pearl region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the binary structural-information prototype that a multivalued coarsening theorem should recover as a special case.

method_exemplars.technique: Express non-descendant, back-door, and mediator information as modular counterfactual-distribution constraints while isolating the mediator-induced bilinear equalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization must preserve this program's identified set while replacing its nonconvex mediator component.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain endpoint inference from finite active representations and directional derivatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An exact finite linear or convex reduction could expose active endpoint pieces and make tie-aware limit theory possible for mediator-tightened bounds.

literature_map:
Pearl (1999, Synthese) introduced PN, PS, and PNS as distinct counterfactual aspects of causation.
Tian and Pearl (2000, Annals of Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence) derived sharp binary PoC bounds from common-population observational and experimental data using response-type linear programming.
Li and Pearl (2024, AAAI, doi:10.1609/aaai.v38i18.30030) extended PoCs to nonbinary treatments and outcomes but described most recursive bounds as not known to be tight.
Shu, Wang, and Li (2026, IJCAI, arXiv:2505.15274) reduced discrete PoCs to four representative families and produced closed-form bounds; all-dimensional validity is proved, while universal tightness is supported computationally in low dimensions and remains open.
Xie and Li (2026, UAI workshop) supplied an explicit every-margin constructive tightness proof for binary PNS and identified nonnegative solvability of enlarged response systems as the nonbinary obstruction.
Koperberg (2024, Statistics & Probability Letters, arXiv:2202.02092) connects finite Strassen couplings, Hall conditions, and matchings, providing transferable flow-and-cut machinery.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) and generic response-signature programs show that broad counterfactual bounds can be computed numerically but do not provide compact all-alphabet PoC endpoint laws.
Mueller, Li, and Pearl (2022, IJCAI, doi:10.24963/ijcai.2022/376) show how graph, covariate, and mediator information can tighten binary causes-of-effects bounds.
Xie and Li (2026, arXiv:2602.14503) extend partial-diagram PoC programs to finite alphabets; covariate programs are linear, whereas mediator independences generate bilinear nonconvex constraints.
Shu, Lei, and Li (2026, arXiv:2608.12657) derive multivalued bounds using covariate and mediator knowledge, exposing a sharpness-versus-tractability frontier beyond the common-population base model.
Xie and Li (2026, Technical Report R-29) derive tight incomplete-subpopulation bounds for binary variables and leave the exponentially larger nonbinary closed-form problem open.
Cheng, Mao, Pearl, and Li (2026, arXiv:2602.17070) provide regular and directional delta-method inference for finite affine PoC envelopes; the guarantees are asymptotic and the worked PoC cases binary.
Horowitz and Lee (arXiv:1905.06491), Stoye (2009, Econometrica), and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica) provide adjacent partial-identification inference machinery but not exact all-alphabet block-multinomial PoC inversion.
Harinen, Iliev, Li, Mueller, and Zhang (2022, KDD Customer Journey Optimization Workshop) illustrate the common-population experimental-plus-observational customer-journey use case through binary necessary-and-sufficient intervention examples.
The central tension is that explicit multivalued affine bounds and generic exponential LP certificates exist, but constructive universal sharpness, scalable witnesses and dual cuts, boundary-safe finite-sample inference, and multivalued incomplete-data analogues do not yet coincide in one theory.
